topic: Explicit Qualification of Namespace Members Declared Outside Their Namespace
explanation: In C++, members of a named namespace can be defined outside the namespace block by explicitly qualifying them with the namespace name. This allows separation of declaration and definition, which is useful for organizing code, especially in large projects or when implementing functions outside class or namespace definitions. The explicit qualification ensures the compiler correctly associates the definitions with their declared namespace members, provided the definitions occur after the declaration within an enclosing namespace scope.
